correctness.rationale: On the exact frozen four-crossing Hamiltonian three-zone family, outer first-return branches are reflections with derivative -1. The two central energy equations give At=Bu and 2D+b_C(t²-u²)=0; the isolation hypothesis excludes A=B and A=B=0, hence AB>0 and A≠B. Central section derivatives yield Q=(A-b_Ct)(B+b_Cu)/((B-b_Cu)(A+b_Ct)) with forward multiplier μ=Q^sgn(b_C). The central normal velocities are opposite across each switching section, so the denominator in Q−1 is strictly negative and sign(μ−1)=sign(B−A). Thus every such isolated crossing cycle is hyperbolic, attractive iff B<A. Independently factored Q−1 symbolically and recomputed the published exact quadratic-field example μ≈7.163689825174318, reverse-time reciprocal≈0.139592866861. These finite tests are illustrative; the energy/reflection/saltation argument supplies the universal proof.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks do not establish the universal theorem without the analytical/chain argument given; code proof obligations were reconstructed separately.
